newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu plans to cede 40 pct of West Bank - report.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu plans to cede 40 pct of West Bank - report.

text.p: Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu plans to offer the Palestinians control of about 40 percent of the West Bank in a final peace deal, the newspaper Haaretz said on Thursday.

News of a secret plan angered Palestinians who expect that a final accord due to be completed by May 1999 will give them a state in nearly all of the West Bank captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

"These numbers -- excuse the expression -- are political masturbation by the government of Israel," Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat's adviser Ahmed Tibi told Israeli army radio, suggesting Israelis should negotiate with Palestinians rather than juggling figures among themselves.

Netanyahu acknowledged in radio interviews having some ideas about a final peace deal and said they were discussed in his inner cabinet for the first time on Wednesday when the military presented its security assessments.
But he said: "I haven't shown anyone or drafted any map."
The newspaper published a detailed front-page illustration of what it called "Netanyahu's map". Asked if he had a map, Netanyahu told Israel Radio: "A map in the head? Who doesn't have one?"

Israel already has handed over much of the Gaza Strip, seven West Bank cities and part of an eighth to self-rule under peace deals launched in 1993. More than two million Palestinians live in the West Bank and Gaza.

Netanyahu said Egyptian envoy Osama al-Baz would brief him on talks the envoy had on Wednesday with Arafat to revive Middle East peacemaking stuck for two months over Jewish settlement building in the West Bank.
The meeting was due to take place at 1630 GMT.
"The secret map which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intends to present to the Palestinian Authority in final-status negotiations would give them less than 40 percent of the area," Haaretz said.
The report by military commentator Ze'ev Schiff said various details had yet to be worked out and the "Netanyahu map" was open to negotiation.

"The Palestinians will be told all the same that if the security situation will allow it over time, some security arrangements will be eased, and thus will the Palestinian entity get additional territories in the West Bank," it said.

Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that as much as 60 percent of the West Bank would be turned over to the Palestinians under a proposal the security establishment presented to the cabinet ministers.
Asked which newspaper report to believe, Netanyahu told Israeli army radio: "I suggest that you not always believe what you read in the newspapers."
"I didn't specify any number," he said and added: "I have my own ideas." He said the discussion which began in the inner cabinet on Wednesday would continue during a series of meetings to come.
Tibi said he believed the policy of the Netanyahu government elected a year ago was leading the Middle East to a greater confrontation than the Palestinian intifada, or uprising, that ended in 1993.
Tibi called the proposal published by Haaretz "a shot with automatic fire at the dying body of the Oslo accord" which launched Israeli-PLO peace moves four years ago.
"Benjamin Netanyahu is successfully destroying this process," Tibi told army radio.

For all the Palestinian anger at anything short of an independent state, the reported map appeared to represent another nail in the coffin of a right-wing religious dream of a Jewish state in all of biblical Israel.
Haaretz said about half of Netanyahu's cabinet ministers backed the proposal to cede 40 percent of the West Bank.
National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon said the map, as reported, was little different from one he had conceived nearly 20 years ago.
